issues.description: Indentation bug places `if sys.version_info >= (3, 11):` adjacent to `Math_unary` class and rebinds the class name
issues.detail: In `numba/core/typing/mathdecl.py`, the diff removes the blank line that separated the `Math_unary` class from the following `@infer_global(math.atan2)` decorator. More importantly, `Math_unary = infer_global(math.exp2)(Math_unary)` reassigns the module-level name `Math_unary`. That complects two concerns into one mutable name: the template definition and the registration of a second global. The simple move is to register without rebinding: `infer_global(math.exp2)(Math_unary)` as a statement, no assignment.

issues.description: Version gate is duplicated across three files instead of expressed once as data
issues.detail: `sys.version_info >= (3, 11)` appears in `mathdecl.py`, `cpython/mathimpl.py`, `np/math/mathimpl.py`, and the test file (as `PYVERSION >= (3, 11)`). The fact 'math.exp2 exists on Python >= 3.11' is one value about the world, repeated four times. That is place-oriented programming applied to a fact. The simple form is one predicate — `HAS_MATH_EXP2 = hasattr(math, 'exp2')` — defined once and referenced everywhere. `hasattr` is also more honest: the actual question is 'does this symbol exist', not 'what Python version is this'.

issues.description: `numba/cpython/mathimpl.py` and `numba/np/math/mathimpl.py` reference `sys` without an import shown in the diff
issues.detail: The diff adds `if sys.version_info >= (3, 11):` to both `mathimpl.py` files but the diff context does not show a `sys` import being added. If `sys` is already imported at module top, fine; if not, this is a NameError at import time on every Python version. Verify both files import `sys` at module scope. This is incidental complexity created entirely by the version-check approach — `hasattr(math, 'exp2')` needs no new import.

issues.description: Release note file missing trailing newline
issues.detail: `docs/upcoming_changes/10276.new_feature.rst` ends with `\ No newline at end of file`. Incidental, but the kind of thing that fails a docs lint and creates noise downstream.

issues.description: Test x_values do not exercise the distinguishing behavior of exp2
issues.detail: The test reuses the exp test's `x_values = [-2, -1, -2, 2, 1, 2, .1, .2]`. For `exp2`, values like `0`, `1`, `2`, `10` are exactly the inputs where exp2 differs cleanly from exp (powers of two give exact integers). Including at least one such value would test that the LLVM intrinsic is in fact `exp2` and not accidentally wired to `exp`. The value of a test is the bug it would catch; this test would not catch a copy-paste of the wrong intrinsic name.

issues.description: Duplicate value `-2` in test inputs (copy-pasted from exp test)
issues.detail: `x_values = [-2, -1, -2, 2, 1, 2, .1, .2]` contains `-2` and `2` twice. Harmless but reveals that the test was cloned from `test_exp` without thought — exactly what the lens calls TDD-as-design without the design step. The easy move was to copy; the simple move was to ask 'what values actually exercise exp2?'

review.summary: The change is small and correct in shape — wire `math.exp2` through the same `unary_math_intr` machinery as `math.exp`, gated by Python version. What's complected is the version-gating: one fact about the world ('exp2 exists on 3.11+') is repeated as four separate `sys.version_info` and `PYVERSION` checks across four files, when it should be one named predicate (preferably `hasattr(math, 'exp2')`, which is the actual question). The `Math_unary = infer_global(...)(Math_unary)` rebinding in `mathdecl.py` needlessly mutates a module-level name; the registration side-effect is what's wanted, not the reassignment. Also verify `sys` is imported in both `mathimpl.py` files — the diff does not show the import being added, and a missing import here is a hard failure. The test reuses the `exp` input values verbatim, which means it would not detect the most obvious wiring bug (wrong intrinsic name); add an input or two where `exp2` produces a clean integer to make the test actually do work.
